zones.name: Practice zone: receiving, main floor and charging area

inspectables.area: Receiving floor, between dock doors and the racks
inspectables.cue: A dark, glossy patch about two meters across on the concrete; the surrounding floor is matte. The sheen catches the high-bay lights.
inspectables.label: Oil or fluid spill
inspectables.why: A spill on a walking route is a classic slip hazard: moderate likelihood (traffic is high) and high severity (head and back injuries are common in same-level falls). Immediate control: cordon and clean; higher-level control: fix the leaking truck or container that caused it.
inspectables.hintWarm: Look down where people walk, not at the racks.

inspectables.area: Receiving dock, trailer at the open door
inspectables.cue: A trailer is backed up to an open dock door. The dock signal beside the door shows red, meaning the trailer is not secured to the dock.
inspectables.label: Trailer not secured at the dock
inspectables.why: A trailer that creeps away from the dock while a truck drives in can drop the truck to the ground: rare, but potentially fatal. Before anyone drives onto it, the trailer should be secured to the dock and the signal should show green. Better control: a vehicle restraint interlocked with the dock door (engineering), so the door can't open until the trailer is held.
inspectables.hintWarm: Look at the signal light beside the open dock door.

inspectables.area: Main floor walkway, near the yellow lines
inspectables.cue: A dark hose is stretched diagonally across the marked pedestrian walkway, low to the ground.
inspectables.label: Hose across the walkway
inspectables.why: Anything across a marked walkway trips people whose eyes are up (listening for trucks). High likelihood, medium severity. Control: route hoses overhead or through ramps (engineering), not 'watch your step' signs.
inspectables.hintWarm: Follow the yellow line from the dock. Is it clear the whole way?

inspectables.area: Charging area, charger on the west wall
inspectables.cue: Where the charging cable meets the plug, the insulation is split and three strands poke out at an angle.
inspectables.label: Frayed charger supply cable
inspectables.why: Damaged insulation on the charger's mains supply cable risks electric shock, and charging areas are occupied during shift changes. Lower likelihood, very high severity. Control: take the charger out of service and replace the cable; interim: lockout and a tag.
inspectables.hintWarm: Look closely at the ends of the charging cable, where it bends.

inspectables.area: Charging area, floor next to the charger
inspectables.cue: A cable lies on the floor, but it passes through a yellow rubber cable ramp that covers it.
inspectables.label: Ramped charging cable
inspectables.why: Looks like a trip risk, but the cable is protected by a proper cable ramp and sits outside the marked walkway. Controlled condition — no action needed beyond keeping the ramp seated.

inspectables.cue: A pallet stack about three meters tall of cartons, fully wrapped in clear shrink wrap and squared on the pallet.
inspectables.label: Wrapped tall pallet stack
inspectables.why: Height looks alarming, but the load is shrink-wrapped to the pallet and squared, so cartons cannot slide. Controlled condition — this is how tall stacks are supposed to look.

inspectables.cue: A reach truck is parked beside the charging area, mast lowered, keys removed (a red card on the cab shows lockout).
inspectables.label: Parked reach truck
inspectables.why: A parked truck with the mast down and keys controlled is not itself a hazard to flag during a walk-through; its movement patterns matter in the incident replay instead.

zones.name: Assessed zone: racking aisle and packing station

inspectables.area: Aisle, east rack row, second beam level
inspectables.cue: One pallet juts past the front edge of the beam, rotated slightly, overhanging the aisle by roughly half a meter.
inspectables.label: Pallet overhanging the beam
inspectables.why: An overhanging pallet sits at head height for a driver and can be struck or dropped by the next truck through the aisle. The incident replay starts exactly here. Immediate: restack the pallet now. Lasting fix: load stops on the beam (an engineering control); a put-away quality check backs that up.
inspectables.hintCold: Compare each pallet's front edge with its beam.

inspectables.area: Aisle, south rack row, first upright
inspectables.cue: One blue rack upright is bent inward at mid-height and the paint has scuffed to bare orange metal at the impact point.
inspectables.label: Bent rack upright
inspectables.why: A damaged upright can collapse under load with no warning; racking failures are catastrophic. It must be offloaded and repaired by a qualified person. Control: engineer it — column guards and barrier railing at aisle ends reduce recurrence.
inspectables.hintCold: Stand back and sight along each upright: straight lines hide dents less well.

inspectables.cue: Two pallets of cartons are staged directly in front of a green exit sign and door.
inspectables.label: Blocked fire exit
inspectables.why: Exit routes must be kept free and unobstructed; US OSHA's exit-route rule (29 CFR 1910.37(a)(3)) says no materials or equipment may be placed in them, even temporarily. A blocked exit is low-frequency but fatal when it is needed. Control: marked staging areas (engineering the layout) plus a housekeeping standard.
inspectables.hintCold: Check every green sign. Can a person reach each one without climbing?

inspectables.area: Aisle, north end, pole-mounted convex mirror
inspectables.cue: The convex mirror at the blind corner is aimed at the ceiling structure, not the cross-aisle it should reflect.
inspectables.label: Misaligned convex mirror
inspectables.why: A mirror aimed at nothing gives false confidence at a blind corner — drivers believe they have checked when they have not. This is a maintenance-system issue as much as a training one; see the 'Is it training?' page.
inspectables.hintCold: What should each mirror show, and what does it actually show?

inspectables.area: Packing bench, cutting machine, near side
inspectables.cue: The cutting machine's orange guard rail is missing on the operator side; the far side still has its guard.
inspectables.label: Missing machine guard
inspectables.why: An unguarded cutting edge at a busy bench risks lacerations and amputations. Interim control: tag out. Better: interlocked guard (engineering) so the machine cannot run unprotected.
inspectables.hintCold: Compare the two sides of the machine.

inspectables.area: Aisle, south rack row, top level
inspectables.cue: A carton stack on the top beam leans about 12 degrees off vertical, unwrapped.
inspectables.label: Leaning unwrapped stack
inspectables.why: Unwrapped cartons leaning on a high beam fall into the aisle or onto a truck. Control: restack and re-band; the deeper fix is the put-away quality check that let it leave the wrap station.
inspectables.hintCold: Look at verticals: pallet edges, uprights, box corners.

inspectables.area: Packing bench, cutting machine, far side
inspectables.cue: The far side of the same machine has its orange guard rail fitted and closed.
inspectables.label: Guarded side of the machine
inspectables.why: The exposed-looking blade area on this side is behind a fixed guard. A machine that looks dangerous but is guarded is a controlled condition — the inspection question is whether every side is guarded.

inspectables.area: Aisle, floor between the rack rows
inspectables.cue: The aisle floor between the rack rows is clear: nothing stored or spilled on it.
inspectables.label: Clear aisle floor
inspectables.why: Not everything in a busy warehouse is wrong. Knowing what is acceptable keeps reporting credible.

zones.name: Transfer zone: outbound staging lane (no hints)

inspectables.cue: A pallet in the staging lane is stacked so high the driver cannot see over it, and it is parked straddling the yellow walkway line.
inspectables.label: Loaded truck straddling the walkway
inspectables.why: Both an obstructed-view vehicle and a blocked walkway: pedestrians must pass around a machine they cannot see the operator of. Control: keep the staging lane clear of the walkway (layout) and require high-load travel in reverse where vision is blocked.

inspectables.cue: The battery-change bay door is blocked by a wheeled cage, and the eyewash station beside it has an empty wash bottle on top.
inspectables.label: Blocked battery bay and neglected eyewash
inspectables.why: Emergency equipment that is unreachable or unmaintained fails exactly when it is needed. Where people can be splashed by corrosive battery electrolyte, US OSHA (29 CFR 1910.151(c)) expects quick-drenching or eye-flushing facilities in the work area. Control: a weekly emergency-equipment check owned by a named role.

inspectables.cue: A black-and-yellow striped swing gate partially closes the lane entrance.
inspectables.label: Striped swing gate at the lane entrance
inspectables.why: Stripes read as 'danger', but a self-closing gate at a vehicle route is a control, not a hazard — it separates pedestrians from trucks.

inspectables.cue: The yellow walkway through the staging lane is clear and unbroken except at the gate.
inspectables.label: Clear walkway
inspectables.why: A correct condition: no action needed.
